records.name: Li Chen
records.evidenceNote: Cornell vita: Ph.D. Management Science and Engineering, Stanford University, June 2005. Industry positions: Walmart.com supply chain consultant 06/2004-09/2004 (a summer post during the doctorate), then TrueDemand Software cofounder and lead scientist 09/2004-03/2008; academic positions begin with Duke Fuqua Assistant Professor 07/2008. TrueDemand began nine months before the June 2005 degree (overlap stated), in the final year of the doctorate rather than throughout it, and was not changed on completion; it continued for almost three years after the degree, so under the 17 October rule for a post begun a few months before the thesis was finished (Brynjolfsson precedent, eight months) it is the first job and keeps its own 2004 start year. If the integrator instead treats it as a pre-degree job continued after the degree, the first new job is Duke, Assistant Professor, July 2008 (tenure-track). Verifier (no field changed): the Cornell vita, re-opened on 2026-10-17, lists TrueDemand Software, Cofounder and Lead Scientist, 09/2004-03/2008, with no title change, the Walmart.com supply chain consultancy 06/2004-09/2004 and IBM research internships in 2003 before it, the Stanford Ph.D. dated June 2005, and Duke Fuqua Assistant Professor from 07/2008. Keeping the 2004 TrueDemand start is consistent with the published Brynjolfsson row and the verified Ying Kei (Mike) Tse row (posts begun about eight months before the degree or thesis submission and not retitled). The thesis submission month is not known. If the integrator instead treats a company role begun in the final doctoral year as a pre-degree job continued under rule 1, the first new job is Duke, July 2008, Assistant Professor at a business school (tenure-track by convention). Integrator (2026-10-17): kept as recorded after the integrator check proposed Duke 2008. Rule 1 covers a job begun well before the degree; a post begun in the final year of the doctorate and not changed on completion keeps its own start year under the rule for posts not retitled, which is applied to posts outside academia too (David Gamarnik: IBM Research from 1997 for a February 1998 degree), and nine months matches the accepted Brynjolfsson, Dhar and Piramuthu leads.

records.name: Jan van Dalen
records.employer: Erasmus University Rotterdam (Rotterdam School of Management)
records.evidenceNote: His self-entered ORCID employment record gives RSM Erasmus University, Technology and Operations Management, from 1992-09 (entered under his current title, Associate professor of Statistics), and the later Pure-sourced entries continue at the same department from 2009. The EUR Pure record of his doctoral thesis 'Quantitative Studies in Wholesaling' (supervisors Roy Thurik and Koerts; marked externally published) gives the award date 3 December 1992. The RSM post therefore began about three months before the defence (overlap noted); no earlier employment is listed. The starting title is not documented, so position is null and the category unknown. Verifier: kept. His ORCID works list includes a 1988 EIM research publication and a 1990 chapter in a Statistics Netherlands (CBS) volume, and the Pure thesis record lists him under an external organisation, which is consistent with pre-degree work outside RSM; no opened source shows an RSM post before September 1992 or a pre-degree job continuing after the December 1992 defence. Consistency check (2026-10-17): placementYear changed from 1992 to null because the RSM post began in September 1992, about three months before the 3 December 1992 thesis award, and its starting title is undocumented: the ORCID public API (re-read 2026-10-17) dates the RSM entry from 1992-09 only under his present title (Associate professor of Statistics), and the RSM, ERIM and Pure pages give no dated title history. It therefore cannot be told whether a pre-degree title was converted on completion (the converted post, from December 1992 or later, would be the first job) or whether the post simply continued (September 1992). Erasmus University Rotterdam (RSM) is the first employer after the degree either way (John Vande Vate precedent). The 1990 International Journal of Research in Marketing article (RePub) gives his affiliation then as the Econometric Institute, Erasmus University, as part of a workgroup project there, consistent with doctoral research outside RSM; it states no title or contract. Employer, position and category unchanged.

records.name: Mevludin Memedi
records.evidenceNote: His Alfaisal faculty-portal biography states he earned a PhD in Information Technology from Örebro University in 2014 and that, following his doctoral studies, he held a tenure-track position in Computer Engineering at Dalarna University, later serving as Assistant Professor in Informatics at Örebro University. The start year of the Dalarna post is not given; his ORCID dates the Örebro senior lectureship from April 2016. Integrator: the evidence writes the doctorate-awarding institution as 'Örebro University', the same university as the record's 'Örebro University, Sweden', so it is stored under the record's name. Audit (2026-10-17): evidenceNote changed from no statement of a pre-degree Dalarna role to this statement, because the overlap must be recorded (R3: the earlier role is kept in the note). A South East European University news item of 26 April 2010 says that after his 2009 Dalarna master's (best master's thesis prize) he 'was admitted to the Swedish University as the only Albanian young assistant', and Libris shows the 2014 Örebro doctoral thesis also registered in Dalarna University's repository (urn:nbn:se:du-13797), so he held a junior post, apparently at Dalarna, and a Dalarna affiliation during the 2010-2014 doctorate. The title and terms of that post (doctoral studentship, assistant or adjunct) are not given. The bio presents the tenure-track Computer Engineering post as following the doctoral studies, so the row treats it as the post given on completion (R3), start year unknown. If the 2010 post was a regular job rather than a doctoral-stage role, R5 would apply instead, and the first new employer would be Örebro University (Senior Lecturer from 2016-04, ORCID). Consistency check (2026-10-17): placementYear changed from null to 2014, position from null to 'Assistant Professor (tenure track)' and evidenceUrl from https://fp.alfaisal.edu/profile/mmemedi to his Alfaisal CV, because the CV (March 2026 version; the February 2024 version has the same entries), read in its work-experience and education sections, dates the Dalarna posts: 'PhD student', Dalarna University, Borlänge, from 2010 (80% research for the doctoral education, 20% teaching), then 'Assistant Professor (tenure track)', Dalarna University, from 2014, then Örebro University Business School from 2016, with the Örebro PhD in Information Technology in 2014 (an IT consultancy at Nordforce Technology from 2008 precedes the doctoral post). The 2010 post was therefore a doctoral studentship, a doctoral-stage role and not a regular job, so the alternative reading above (Örebro as the first new employer) does not apply; the Dalarna tenure-track assistant professorship from 2014 is the first post-PhD job, and because the CV states the tenure track the category stays tenure-track.

records.evidenceNote: University of Cologne profile states that in 2007 he received a Ph.D. in Computer Science from the University of Minnesota and started as an Assistant Professor at RSM, Erasmus University; promoted to Associate Professor (early tenure) in 2011 and Full Professor in July 2013; chaired professor at Cologne since 2017. The RSM and EUR profiles say he has been affiliated with RSM since 2007 and began his academic career there as an Assistant Professor. Start month not documented. Audit (2026-10-17): category changed from tenure-track to unknown because neither the plain-title convention (North American or Asian business or engineering schools) nor the source supports a tenure-track post, after two independent classifiers and a reviewer who re-opened the evidence: RSM is in the Netherlands, where the design rule keeps continental European assistant-professor titles unknown unless the source states the tenure track. The Cologne page says he 'started as an Assistant Professor at the Rotterdam School of Management' and was 'promoted to Associate Professor in 2011 (early tenure)'. That strongly suggests a tenure-track post, but it states tenure for the 2011 promotion, not the contract type of the 2007 assistant professorship. The RSM and EUR profiles use no tenure wording at all. Because the evidence implies the track without stating it, the resolver rule (answer false when unsettled) applies. A source that explicitly calls the 2007 post tenure-track would change this to true.

records.name: John Vande Vate
records.employer: Georgia Institute of Technology (School of Industrial and Systems Engineering)
records.evidenceNote: The Georgia Tech College of Engineering list of July-September 2024 service anniversaries lists 'Vande Vate, John, Professor, Industrial & Systems Engr, 9/17/84' among 40-year anniversaries, so his continuous Georgia Tech service began on 17 September 1984; he remained at Georgia Tech (now Professor Emeritus). DSpace@MIT records his Ph.D. thesis 'The linear matroid parity problem' (advisor James B. Orlin) with copyright 1984 and issue date 1985, and the Mathematics Genealogy Project dates the MIT Ph.D. 1985. The scanned thesis on DSpace@MIT gives the degree as February 1985 on its title page, with the author signature dated 10 October 1984, and its abstract page says it was submitted to the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science in October 1984, so the Georgia Tech service began about three weeks before the thesis was submitted and about five months before the February 1985 conferral. His starting title is not stated (the list gives his 2024 rank), so position and category are unknown. Verifier: placementYear corrected from 1984 to null. The thesis title and abstract pages show the dissertation was not yet submitted when the Georgia Tech service began on 17 September 1984, so the one-year allowance does not apply; whether the 1984 start is the first-job start (a post not retitled on completion) or a pre-degree title that Georgia Tech converted on completion (the converted post, starting 1985 or later, would then be the first job) depends on his starting title, which no source states. Georgia Tech as the first employer after the degree is unaffected.

records.name: Mark Embrechts
records.evidenceNote: The RPI profile says he joined the Nuclear Engineering Department at Rensselaer in 1983 and was previously an AWU-DOE fellow, staff member and Laboratory Director's Fellow at Los Alamos National Laboratory (1981-1983). Math Genealogy gives his Virginia Tech PhD as 1981. The three Los Alamos roles are not separately dated, so the first post-PhD title and kind of post (postdoctoral Director's Fellow or staff member) are not established; the employer is, but the 1981 start belongs to the pre-degree AWU-DOE thesis fellowship (see the audit statement). Integrator: the evidence writes the doctorate-awarding institution as 'Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University', the same university as the record's 'Virginia Tech', so it is stored under the record's name. Audit (2026-10-17): placementYear changed from 1981 to null because the 1981 start belongs to a pre-degree role (R3/R7). Los Alamos issued his dissertation as thesis report LA-9232-T (February 1982), read through the r.jina.ai reader proxy because sgp.fas.org served a bot challenge. The report says the thesis was accepted by Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University for the Ph.D. and that the work was supported by the DOE Office of Fusion Energy and Associated Western Universities. Its acknowledgements thank Associated Western Universities for 'the A. W. U. fellowship, which made his stay at the Los Alamos National Laboratory possible' (specially funded by the DOE Office of Fusion Energy) and Dr. D. J. Dudziak of Los Alamos for daily supervision. It also cites a private communication of June 1981. The AWU-DOE fellowship was therefore the graduate fellowship under which he wrote the thesis at Los Alamos, still in progress in mid-1981. His first post-PhD role at Los Alamos (staff member or Laboratory Director's Fellow) began after the 1981 degree, at an undated point before the 1983 move to RPI. This is a pre-degree post followed by a regular post at the same laboratory, not a job held through the doctorate. Employer kept; position null and category unknown unchanged.

records.name: Erik Brynjolfsson
records.employer: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Sloan School of Management)
records.evidenceNote: His June 2020 CV (Stanford Profiles download) dates the MIT Sloan Ph.D. in Managerial Economics 9/86 - 2/91 and lists MIT Sloan Assistant Professor 6/1990 - 6/1995, after MIT Sloan research assistant 9/1986 - 6/1990; the part-time Harvard instructor role ran 9/1985 - 9/1994, beginning well before the degree. The assistant professorship started about eight months before the February 1991 degree date (overlap noted). The GSB profile lists the same period as 'Associate Professor, MIT Sloan School, 1990-1995', which conflicts with the CV's dated Assistant (1990-1995) and Associate (1995-2001) entries. Integrator: the evidence writes the doctorate-awarding institution as 'MIT', the same university as the record's 'Massachusetts Institute of Technology', so it is stored under the record's name. Audit (2026-10-17): placementYear changed from 1990 to 1991 because the one-year allowance of R2 needs a start after the dissertation was complete, and the MIT thesis shows it was not complete in June 1990. MIT DSpace holds the thesis (hdl 1721.1/13687), read from rendered page images of the scanned PDF. Its title page reads 'Submitted to the School of Management ... September, 1990' and the abstract page says it was submitted on September 15, 1990. The Sloan Ph.D. Committee chair's acceptance is dated 9/27/90 and the MIT Libraries Archives stamp 4 October 1990. DSpace dates the degree 1991 (copyright 1990), matching the CV's February 1991 degree. The assistant professorship (June 1990 - June 1995, no title change in the CV) therefore began about three and a half months before the dissertation was submitted. Following the Buket Avci treatment of an assistant professorship begun before the dissertation was finished, the job is kept and placementYear is 1991, the year he first held the post with the degree (February 1991); the June 1990 start stays in this note. Employer, position and category unchanged. Integrator (17 October 2026): placementYear kept at 1990, the documented start (June 1990) of the MIT assistant professorship. The post was not retitled when the thesis was submitted in September 1990, so the conversion rule does not apply and 1991 would not be the start year of any job; the assistant professorship is the first job, begun about three months before thesis submission and eight months before the February 1991 degree (overlap).

It therefore cannot be told whether a pre-degree title was converted on completion (the converted post, from conferral or later, would be the first job) or the post simply continued (August 2019).
